inferencesNotProof: This pattern is consistent with an aggregate VM uncached-throughput bottleneck after the initial burst: D2s_v4 documentation lists 48 MB/s uncached throughput and 200 MB/s uncached burst throughput; the replay-tail DATA LUN median was about 48.8 MB/s while the VM-level bandwidth metric was saturated.

The per-disk DATA bandwidth metric was only around 47% on the replay tail and WAL LUN throughput use was near zero, while the VM-wide bandwidth metric was saturated. This is consistent with shared VM-path contention affecting replay/WAL I/O, rather than a single replay process being the sole limiter, but it cannot prove the exact causal mechanism.
limits: Azure Monitor platform metrics are minute-level aggregates. VM uncached bandwidth is VM-wide and does not attribute traffic to PostgreSQL or external reader processes; disk LUN metrics show device activity but not process ownership. Do not subtract external-reader I/O from the observed guest/OS device totals.

D2s_v4 documentation expresses the 48 MB/s/200 MB/s figures for uncached Premium SSD. This stack used Standard_LRS HDD. The size-level cap is a strong consistency check, not a guarantee that each Standard HDD workload maps exactly to that spec row.
The run ended at 3 hours with replay incomplete. Existing WAL-slot evidence says later local replay is not proof that new WAL was received.
observations: During the 144-minute replay tail, VM uncached bandwidth consumed averaged 99.71% (median 100.0%, 144/144 minute buckets); VM uncached IOPS consumed averaged 1.28% (median 1.0%).

Replica DATA LUN 0 read bandwidth was 96.94 MB/s mean during VACUUM and 53.56 MB/s mean (48.79 MB/s median) during replay tail; its per-disk bandwidth-consumed metric fell from 95.5% to 51.7% while VM-wide uncached bandwidth stayed near 100%.

Replica WAL LUN 1 replay-tail read throughput was 69.8 kB/s mean; its bandwidth/IOPS consumed percentages averaged 0.0%/0.0%. Yet Azure Data Disk Latency for WAL LUN 1 averaged 3090 ms (median 3428 ms), with queue depth 1.80 mean. The PostgreSQL guest monitor separately showed WAL read-await around 3.4 s.

The Azure API returned 195 one-minute buckets through 04:34Z for the requested 01:20Z–04:35Z window. After the SIGINT, only five extra buckets remain; they are observational tail and do not establish continued WAL reception or completed replay.
